To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the knowledge, skills, and resources for pharmacy informatics education should be based on the medication use process, should be taught in all doctor of pharmacy programs and in continuing education, and should be updated to reflect changes in practice.

pharmacy informatics education should be conceptualized within the medication use process and should include the following: (1) the ability to identify and apply appropriate technology to support the medication use process; (2) an understanding of the role of pharmacy informatics in the medication use process as well as an understanding of the impact of technology on patient care, including the potential for error; (3) the ability to communicate effectively and appropriately with other healthcare professionals about pharmacy informatics and technology use; (4) the

pharmacy students must have a basic knowledge and understanding of pharmacy informatics, and that the curriculum should provide students with the opportunity to develop the skills necessary to effectively use pharmacy informatics to support the medication use process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to prepare future pharmacy practitioners for a world in which pharmacy informatics is ubiquitous and essential for safe and effective medication management.
the identification of core competencies for pharmacy informatics and the development of a curriculum to support their attainment.
identifying core knowledge and skills in the discipline of pharmacy informatics and developing an evidence-based framework for pharmacy informatics education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a need for a more standardized approach to the teaching of pharmacy informatics in pharmacy education.
there is a need for a comprehensive pharmacy informatics curriculum.
pharmacy informatics is the study of pharmaceutical care and related clinical, educational, and research activities as applied to the management of patient information and communication systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

pharmacy informatics education is a critical component for pharmacy students, regardless of their future practice model, and that the content and learning activities described herein should be considered for incorporation into the curricula of all pharmacy programs.
pharmacy informatics is an essential component of pharmacy education and practice.

the pharmacy informatics curriculum is a work in progress, but we have made great strides toward a common understanding of the core competencies and the knowledge and skills that are necessary for pharmacy practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
all students must have a foundational knowledge and skills in pharmacy informatics, and the profession must work together to ensure this is accomplished.
pharmacy informatics education must be a priority in pharmacy schools.
pharmacy informatics is not an optional component of pharmacy education; rather, it is an integral part of the profession.
